title: paged-kv-cache-block-allocator-reuse-pinning-locality-optimizations
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: the paged KV cache block manager has been a source of tail-latency variability and memory fragmentation under mixed workloads. Motivation: reduce allocator churn, improve locality to avoid cross-device copies, and expose reusable/pinned blocks to the scheduler to improve continuous-batching throughput. Summary: this PR introduces a reuse-first block allocator, locality-aware pinning heuristics, and lightweight allocator metrics. The allocator now keeps LRU reusable bucket lists keyed by block size and device locality so frequently re-requested blocks are recycled instead of reallocated. Pinning is updated to prefer blocks on the originating device and to allow transient pin-with-ttl for active KV ranges. We also reduced lock contention on the hot path using per-shard freelists with try-lock fallbacks. Integration points: scheduler now annotates requests with locality hints so batching groups can co-locate KV accesses when possible. The change preserves the public KV cache API and is backward compatible with existing persisted pages. Checklist: run unit tests, run integration stress tests, run perf canary in perf-canary lab, add allocator metrics to observability pack, add a short note to release notes. Testing performed: unit tests + new allocator tests added, multi-GPU integration stress tests, perf canary runs across g4dn and a100-like instances, fuzz tests for eviction correctness. Results: in our perf canary across representative chat workloads we observed 6-12% throughput improvement for 8k context workloads, 14-18% reduction in p95 token latency, and ~23% reduction in observed device memory fragmentation (measured by peak alloc events); memory churn and allocation syscalls down by ~40% under synthetic reuse patterns. Migration/fallback: non-upgraded schedulers will still function; pinning TTL has safe defaults and falls back to eviction when capacity is constrained. Follow-ups: expose allocator histograms in console dashboards and add a canary that exercises cross-device worst-case patterns.
commits: 3 commits: 1) allocator: introduce reuse buckets and per-shard freelists; 2) pinning: add locality-aware pinWithTTL and heuristics; 3) metrics/tests: expose allocator stats + unit/integration tests
review_conversation: Initial review (Marco) asked for additional allocator metrics and a microbenchmark; author added histograms (allocation_count, reuse_hits, locality_misses) and ran targeted microbenchmarks. Priya requested lock contention numbers and suggested try-lock fallback to avoid priority inversion; implemented per-shard try-lock with graceful fallback and added tests. Daniel flagged a potential race in pin-with-ttl expiry; added a small GC pass and retested. All reviewers approved after addressing comments. Priya performed final review and approved for merge.
ci_checks: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: pass, lint: pass, perf-canary: pass (2/2 stable runs), fuzz: pass, codecov: 89% (allocator files + tests added)
merge_result: squash and merge by Priya Nair on 2026-02-18. Commit message summarized features and perf numbers. No manual conflicts encountered.
release_notes: Paged KV cache: allocator reuse and locality-aware pinning improvements reduce allocation churn and tail latency. Expect 6-12% throughput gains and lower memory fragmentation for multi-GPU workloads. Metrics: allocator.reuse_hits, allocator.locality_misses, allocator.allocation_count exposed for observability.
notes_for_ops: Rolling out to Dedicated clusters via canary channel first. Watch allocator.reuse_hits and allocator.locality_misses; if locality_misses spike, rollback pinning heuristics or increase pin TTL conservatively. Perf canary config and scripts stored in perf-canary repo.
backport_plan: No backport to older branches required for this change. If requested, minimal patch to add reuse buckets without scheduler hints can be cherry-picked to release/* branches.
security_implications: None directly; changes are runtime-only and do not alter crypto/auth paths. Pinning uses existing memory safety primitives. Reviewed by security during PR review.
testing_summary: Added unit tests covering reuse buckets, pin expiry, and concurrency; integration stress test showed stable behavior under 500 concurrent sessions; perf canary across two instance types validated throughput/latency improvements. All tests green in CI.
notes: Follow-up work tracked in ENG-5012 to add allocator heatmaps to the console and in ENG-5091 to expose a scheduler hint API for fine-grained locality control.
